GY6 EFI OBD-2 DTC Fault Codes

ℹ️ This page vs the flash code page: Older GY6 EFI ECUs (KEIHIN PGM-FI clones) communicate faults as blink sequences — no scanner needed. Modern Rongmao, Delphi, and Motion ECUs speak standard OBD-2 DTCs (P0xxx codes) and require an OBD-2 reader. This page covers the OBD-2 / DTC system only.

What You Need

To read and clear fault codes on a Rongmao / Delphi / Motion EFI system you need an OBD-2 reader. The ECU communicates over the K-line (ISO 9141-2) or CAN bus depending on the variant. The following tools are confirmed to work:

  • Car Scanner (Android / iOS) — free app, works with a generic ELM327 Bluetooth or Wi-Fi adapter
  • HUD ECU Hacker (Windows PC) — purpose-built for Rongmao/Delphi GY6 ECUs; allows reading, clearing, and remapping
  • Any generic OBD-2 scanner that supports ISO 9141-2 / KWP2000
⚠️

⚠️ Before reading codes: Check the MIL (malfunction indicator lamp) is working correctly by verifying it illuminates on key-on. Clear any history codes first, then repeat the fault condition and re-read. A code that appears only in history but not as a current fault may have been a one-off transient event.

Reading Codes with Car Scanner

Connect a generic ELM327 Bluetooth or Wi-Fi adapter to the 6-pin OBD-2 diagnostic port (usually under the seat or near the battery). Open Car Scanner (Android / iOS), select the ELM327 adapter, and choose Read fault codes. The app will list any active P-codes — cross-reference them in the DTC table below. Use Clear fault codes after completing your repair to reset the MIL.

Precautions (from Rongmao EFI Owner Manual)

  • Ensure battery positive and negative terminals are reliable and cannot be interchanged. When the engine is running, the battery cannot be disassembled.
  • If the fuel gauge alarm sounds, refuel as soon as possible — the fuel pump cannot operate in air or media other than fuel.
  • Do not arbitrarily disassemble vehicle parts, especially the fuel system (pipeline pressure approx. 250 kPa). Disassembly must be carried out by professional maintenance personnel to prevent fire risk.
  • Do not arbitrarily adjust the throttle valve door plate limit screw. Idle speed on EFI scooters is controlled automatically by the ECU via the IACV.
  • Vehicles may only use the same type of parts specified by the manufacturer. Turn off the ignition switch before disassembly or replacement of any electrical parts.
  • Never pierce the wiring harness to measure signals — use back-probing tools or proper breakout connectors.
  • Ensure the ECU temperature remains below 80 °C.

DTC Reference Table — All Codes

The following OBD-2 P-codes apply to GY6 EFI scooters using Rongmao, Delphi, and Motion injection systems. This table is aligned with the GY6 Injectie Centrum fault code reference and the Rongmao EFI Owner Manual. Detailed step-by-step diagnostic procedures for each code follow below.

DTC CodeComponentFault DescriptionSeverityTypical Symptom
P0107MAP sensorManifold Absolute Pressure — low voltage or open circuitHighRough idle, stalling, poor performance
P0108MAP sensorManifold Absolute Pressure — high voltageHighRich running, black exhaust smoke, poor power
P0112IAT sensorInlet Air Temperature — low voltage or open circuitLowSlightly degraded fuel mapping, rarely noticeable
P0113IAT sensorInlet Air Temperature — high voltageLowSlightly degraded fuel mapping, rarely noticeable
P0117ECT / CTS sensorEngine Coolant/Oil Temperature — low voltage or open circuitMediumPoor cold start enrichment, rough warm-up
P0118ECT / CTS sensorEngine Coolant/Oil Temperature — high voltage or open circuitMediumEngine may over-enrich on warm engine
P0122TPS sensorThrottle Position Sensor — low voltage or open circuitHighSurging, hesitation, possible stalling on acceleration
P0123TPS sensorThrottle Position Sensor — high voltageHighSurging, incorrect fuelling across throttle range
P0131Lambda sensor 1 (O₂S1)Upstream O₂ sensor — low voltage or open circuitMediumLean running, closed-loop fuelling disabled
P0132Lambda sensor 1 (O₂S1)Upstream O₂ sensor — high voltageMediumRich running, closed-loop fuelling disabled
P0031Lambda sensor 1 heaterO₂S1 heater element — low voltage or open circuitMediumSlow O₂ sensor warm-up, open-loop fuelling longer at cold start
P0032Lambda sensor 1 heaterO₂S1 heater element — high voltageMediumShort circuit in heater circuit
P0137Lambda sensor 2 (O₂S2)Downstream O₂ sensor — low voltage or open circuitLowMIL on; emissions monitoring affected
P0138Lambda sensor 2 (O₂S2)Downstream O₂ sensor — high voltageLowMIL on; emissions monitoring affected
P0037Lambda sensor 2 heaterO₂S2 heater element — low voltage or open circuitLowMIL on; heater circuit fault
P0038Lambda sensor 2 heaterO₂S2 heater element — high voltageLowMIL on; short circuit in heater circuit
P0201Fuel injectorInjector cylinder 1 — circuit malfunctionHighEngine will not start or runs very poorly; misfire
P0202Fuel injectorInjector cylinder 2 — circuit malfunctionHighAs P0201 (single-cylinder GY6 scooters only have cylinder 1)
P0230Fuel pump relay (FPR)Fuel pump relay coil — low voltage or open circuitHighNo fuel pump prime on key-on; engine will not start
P0232Fuel pump relay (FPR)Fuel pump relay coil — high voltageHighShort circuit in relay coil circuit
P0351Ignition coilCylinder 1 ignition coil — circuit malfunctionHighNo spark; engine will not start
P0352Ignition coilCylinder 2 ignition coil — circuit malfunctionHighAs P0351 (not applicable on single-cylinder GY6)
P0444PCV / Purge Control ValveEvaporative emission purge control valve — low voltage or open circuitLowMIL on; emissions system affected; drivability usually normal
P0445PCV / Purge Control ValveEvaporative emission purge control valve — high voltageLowMIL on; short circuit in PCV circuit
P0500VSS (Vehicle Speed Sensor)No speed signal detectedMediumSpeedometer inoperative; speed-dependent fuelling maps may be affected
P0505IACV (Idle Air Control Valve)Idle Speed Control — system errorMediumIdle too high, too low, or hunting; stalling at traffic lights
P0562System voltageBattery / charging system voltage — too lowMediumMultiple secondary sensor faults may appear; difficult starting
P0563System voltage / regulatorBattery / charging system voltage — too highHighOvercharging; risk of ECU and battery damage — address immediately
P0650MIL lampMalfunction Indicator Lamp — circuit faultLowMIL lamp itself is defective or its circuit is open/shorted
P0850Neutral switchNeutral position sensor — circuit faultLowIncorrect neutral detection; may affect idle speed in gear
P1693TachometerTachometer signal — low voltage or open circuitLowRev counter inoperative
P1695TachometerTachometer signal — high voltageLowRev counter erratic or pegged
💡

Fault code legend: “Low voltage or open circuit” means the signal at the ECU pin is unexpectedly low — caused by a short to ground, broken wire, or disconnected sensor. “High voltage” means the signal is unexpectedly high — caused by a short to battery, open circuit in the return/ground path, or a failed sensor. Always check connectors and wiring before replacing sensors.

Step-by-Step Diagnostic Procedures

The following procedures are derived from the Rongmao EFI Owner Manual. For each code, follow the numbered steps in order. Connect your OBD-2 diagnostic tool first (Step 1 in every procedure).

P0107 MAP Sensor — Low Voltage or Open Circuit

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check the BARO data — confirm it reads approx. 100 kPa (adjust for altitude).Step 5Next
3Disconnect the MAP sensor connector. Use a multimeter to check voltage between pin 4 and pin 3 of the connector — should be approx. 5 V.Step 5Next
4Check whether pins j2-11, j2-10, j2-16 of the ECU and pins 5, 3, 4 of the connector are shorted to ground.Check the harnessNext
5Start engine and let it idle. Check that MAP reads 30–50 kPa at idle; then open throttle fully (WOT) and confirm MAP rises to approx. 90 kPa.Diagnostic help neededChange the MAP sensor

P0108 MAP Sensor — High Voltage

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check BARO data — confirm approx. 100 kPa.Step 5Next
3Disconnect sensor connector. Check voltage between pin 4 and pin 3 — should be approx. 5 V.Step 5Next
4Check whether pins j2-11, j2-10, j2-16 of the ECU and pins 5, 3, 4 of the connector are shorted to ground.Check the harnessNext
5Start engine at idle. Verify MAP reads 30–50 kPa; at WOT, MAP should reach approx. 90 kPa.Diagnostic help neededChange the MAP sensor

P0112 IAT Sensor — Low Voltage or Open Circuit

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check “intake air temperature” data — confirm it equals the actual ambient temperature.Step 5Next
3Disconnect sensor connector. Use multimeter to check resistance between pin 1 and pin 3 — should be reasonable for the current temperature (see sensor spec table).Step 5Next
4Check voltage between pin 3 and pin 4 of the connector — should be approx. 5 V.NextCheck harness
5Check whether pins j2-8, j2-10 of the ECU and pins 1 and 3 of the connector are shorted to battery.Check the harnessNext
6Start engine and stay at idle. Check that “intake air temperature” rises as the engine warms up.Help neededChange the sensor

P0113 IAT Sensor — High Voltage

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check “intake air temperature” data — confirm it matches actual ambient temperature.Step 5Next
3Disconnect connector. Check resistance between pin 1 and pin 3 matches temperature expectations.Step 5Next
4Check voltage between pin 3 and pin 4 — should be approx. 5 V.NextCheck harness
5Check whether pins j2-8, j2-10 of the ECU and pins 1 and 3 are shorted to battery.Check the harnessNext
6Start engine and idle. Verify “intake air temperature” rises when engine warms up.Help neededChange the sensor

P0117 ECT / CTS Sensor — Low Voltage or Open Circuit

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check “engine temperature” data — confirm it matches actual engine temperature.Step 5Next
3Disconnect sensor connector. Check resistance between pin 1 and pin 2 — should match temperature (e.g. approx. 2.5 kΩ at 20 °C, approx. 300 Ω at 80 °C).Step 5Next
4Check whether pins j2-10, j2-14 of the ECU and pins C and D of the sensor connector are shorted to ground or open.Harness issueNext
5Start engine and idle. Verify “engine temperature” rises as engine gets warm.Help neededChange the sensor

P0118 ECT / CTS Sensor — High Voltage or Open Circuit

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check “engine temperature” data — confirm it matches actual temperature.Step 5Next
3Disconnect connector. Check resistance between pin 1 and pin 2 of the sensor.Step 5Next
4Check whether pins j2-10, j2-14 of the ECU and pins 1 and 2 of the sensor are shorted to ground or open.Harness issueNext
5Start engine and idle. Verify “engine temperature” rises when engine gets warm.Help neededChange the sensor

P0122 TPS — Low Voltage or Open Circuit

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check “Throttle opening” data — confirm it reads 0%–1% at closed throttle.Step 5Next
3Open throttle slowly to 100%. Verify “throttle opening” goes from 0% to 90%–100%.Step 5Next
4Repeat step 3. Check whether the data jumps or skips when opening throttle slowly.Change the sensorNext
5Disconnect connector. Check whether the following pins are shorted to ground or open: j2-12, j2-16 of the ECU and pins 2 and 4 of the sensor.Harness issueNext
6Use multimeter to check voltage between pin 4 and pin 3 of the sensor connector — should be approx. 5 V.Help neededStep 5

P0123 TPS — High Voltage

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Check “Throttle opening” data — should read 0%–1% at closed throttle.Step 5Next
3Open throttle slowly to 100%. Verify data climbs smoothly to 90%–100%.Step 5Next
4Repeat step 3 and check for data jumps when opening throttle.Change the sensorNext
5Disconnect connector. Check whether pins j2-12, j2-16 of the ECU and pins 2 and 4 of the sensor are shorted to ground or open.Harness issueNext
6Check voltage between pin 4 and pin 3 of the sensor — should be approx. 5 V.Help neededStep 5

P0131 / P0132 O₂ Sensor 1 — Low / High Voltage

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Use a multimeter to check the connection between pin B of the oxygen sensor and pin j1-17 of the ECU — is it open? Check whether pin B of the sensor is shorted to pin A.Harness issueNext
3Start engine and warm up. Use multimeter to check whether voltage between pins A and B keeps jumping between 100–900 mV (normal closed-loop switching).Help neededNext
4Check for: A) emission pipe block/leakage; B) injector leakage; C) fuel pressure too high or too low; D) valve clearance too small.Engine maintenance requiredChange the sensor

P0201 Injector 1 — Circuit Malfunction

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Disconnect the injector connector. Use multimeter to check whether the voltage of pin A is approx. 12 V.Step 4Next
3Check whether the connection between pin A and the main power relay is open or shorted to ground.Harness issueNext
4Use multimeter to measure resistance between pin A and pin B of the injector — should be approx. 10–14 Ω at 20 °C.Change the injectorNext
5Use multimeter to check whether the voltage of pin B is approx. 12 V.Help neededNext
6Check whether the connection between pin B of the injector and j2-05 of the ECU is open or shorted to battery/ground.Harness issueHelp needed

P0230 / P0232 Fuel Pump Relay — Low / High Voltage or Open Circuit

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Wait 30 s. Remove the fuel pump relay. Turn ignition on. Check whether the voltage of the relay feeder ear is approx. 12 V.Change the pumpNext
3Check whether the feeder ear is shorted to ground or open.Harness issueHelp needed

P0351 Ignition Coil — Cylinder 1 Circuit Malfunction

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Disconnect the coil connector. Check whether the voltage of pin (+) is approx. 12 V.Step 4Next
3Check whether the connection between pin (+) and the main power relay is open or shorted to ground.Harness issueNext
4Use multimeter to check whether the resistance of the two coil pins is 0.5–0.65 Ω at 20 °C.Change the coilNext
5Use multimeter to check whether voltage of pin B is approx. 12 V.Help neededNext
6Check whether the connection between pin 2 of the coil and j2-01 of the ECU is open or shorted to battery/ground.Harness issueHelp needed

P0505 IACV — Idle Speed Control Error

#OperationYesNo
1Connect the diagnostic tool and turn ignition on.Next—
2Remove the IACV connector. Use multimeter to check resistance between pin A and pin D, and between pin B and pin C — should be approx. 53 ± 5.3 Ω each.NextChange the stepper motor (IACV)
3Check whether all 4 wires of the IACV are shorted to battery/ground or open.Harness issueHelp needed

Symptom-Based Diagnostic Flows

If you cannot read a fault code, or want to verify the code is the root cause, use these symptom-driven checklists directly from the Rongmao EFI Owner Manual.

🚫 Engine Cannot Start

  1. Check battery voltage — should be 8–12 V
  2. Crank engine; check cranking voltage remains above 8 V
  3. Check starter motor operation
  4. In winter: check oil and gearbox oil viscosity
  5. Check engine rotation resistance is not excessive

⚡ Hard / Difficult to Start

  1. Check fuel pump pressure — approx. 250 kPa at idle
  2. Remove spark plug; check spark is normal
  3. Check engine temperature sensor connector and signal
  4. With slightly more throttle, check if engine starts — clean throttle body and bypass channel if yes
  5. Pull injector; crank engine — check injector spray pattern
  6. Check if spark plug is wet (flooding) — dry plug and combustion chamber
  7. Check cylinder compression pressure

〰️ Unstable Idle

  1. Check air filter and intake pipe for leaks or blockage
  2. Check throttle body for carbon deposits in bypass channel
  3. Check IACV operation
  4. Check fuel pressure — approx. 250 kPa
  5. Check injector for blockage
  6. Verify correct spark plug type and condition
  7. Check cylinder compression pressure
  8. Check engine temperature sensor signal
  9. Check TPS signal with throttle at idle

⬆️ High Idle

  1. Check throttle cable for sticking or incorrect adjustment
  2. Check idle pintle adjustment of throttle body
  3. Check intake pipe for air leaks
  4. Check IACV operation
  5. Remove engine temperature sensor; check if engine runs well — change sensor if yes

📉 Poor Acceleration

  1. Check air filter and intake pipe for blockage or leaks
  2. Check fuel pressure — approx. 250 kPa
  3. Remove spark plug — check if wet or dry
  4. Check T-MAP sensor, TPS, and all connectors
  5. Check injector for blockage
  6. Check spark plug type and electrode gap
  7. Check cylinder compression pressure
  8. Check exhaust pipe for blockage

💥 Backfire

  1. Remove spark plug; check spark is normal
  2. Check ignition timing is correct
  3. Check valve clearance for leakage
  4. Check injector for blockage or leaking
  5. Check oxygen sensor operation

Before Starting Fault Analysis — Checklist

From the Rongmao EFI Owner Manual — complete this checklist before beginning any fault code diagnosis:

  1. Confirm the MIL lamp works correctly (illuminates on key-on self-check).
  2. Clear history fault codes, then repeat the fault condition and re-read.
  3. When a new fault code appears, note the exact conditions (hot/cold, idle/acceleration, etc.).
  4. Visually inspect: check for fuel pipe leakage; check for blockage or damage to the intake pipe; check ground connections are secure; check all connectors are properly seated.
  5. If any visual defect is found, repair it first before proceeding with fault code diagnosis.
  6. If no cause is found after completing all steps: do not ignore maintenance items (cylinder pressure, mechanical timing, fuel quality). As a last resort, swap the ECU to test — if the fault disappears, the ECU was the root cause.

Clearing DTCs

On Rongmao / Delphi / Motion systems, codes must be cleared with an OBD-2 scanner — the battery-disconnect method is not guaranteed to clear stored codes on these ECUs (it will reset live data but not always non-volatile fault memory). Use Car Scanner or HUD ECU Hacker to send the “Clear fault codes” command after completing your repair.

⚠️

⚠️ Always repair the root cause first. Clearing a code without fixing the underlying fault will cause it to return within minutes of running the engine.
